subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the DNA double helix, the two antiparallel strands are joined by:
options: hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs
questions.explain: Complementary bases (A-T, G-C) pair via hydrogen bonds; phosphodiester bonds instead link nucleotides along each strand.

questions.q: How many hydrogen bonds form between guanine and cytosine in DNA?
questions.explain: Guanine and cytosine pair via three hydrogen bonds, whereas adenine and thymine pair via two.

options: Favour both extremes against the mean
Favour the intermediate (mean) phenotype and reduce variation
questions.explain: Stabilising selection favours the mean phenotype, selecting against extremes and reducing variation.

questions.q: A student tests a solution with Benedict's reagent and observes no colour change on heating, then performs the Benedict's test again after boiling with dilute acid and neutralising, obtaining a brick-red precipitate. This indicates:
options: a reducing sugar was present originally
a non-reducing sugar such as sucrose was present
questions.explain: Acid hydrolysis breaks a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides, which then give a positive Benedict's result.

questions.q: The Hardy-Weinberg principle predicts that allele and genotype frequencies remain constant only if:
options: There is no mutation, no selection, no migration, random mating and a large population
The population is small with frequent migration
questions.explain: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes a large population with no mutation, selection or migration and random mating.

questions.q: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes whose role is to:
options: break down worn-out organelles, pathogens and cell debris
questions.explain: Lysosomes hold hydrolases that digest unwanted material and engulfed pathogens, recycling cellular components.

questions.q: Genetic drift has the greatest effect on allele frequencies in:
options: Small populations, where chance events strongly affect allele frequencies
questions.explain: In small populations, random chance (drift) can cause large fluctuations in allele frequencies between generations.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes the cell cycle?
questions.explain: Interphase comprises G1 (growth), S (DNA replication) and G2 (preparation), followed by mitosis and cytokinesis.

questions.q: In a DNA nucleotide, the three components are:
questions.explain: A DNA nucleotide consists of a deoxyribose pentose sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base.

questions.q: Courtship behaviour is important in evolution and classification because it:
options: Allows members of the same species to recognise each other and ensures reproductive isolation between species
questions.explain: Species-specific courtship allows recognition of conspecific mates and maintains reproductive isolation between species.

questions.q: Phospholipids form bilayers in water because:
options: both ends of the molecule are hydrophobic
the phosphate head is hydrophilic and the fatty acid tails are hydrophobic
they are entirely hydrophilic and dissolve fully
questions.explain: The amphipathic nature, a hydrophilic phosphate head and hydrophobic tails, drives self-assembly into a bilayer with tails facing inward.

options: A large population is split equally by a barrier
A small group establishes a new population carrying only a subset of the original gene pool
questions.explain: A few founding individuals carry only part of the parent population's genetic variation, skewing allele frequencies in the new population.
